scope: Explicit native shared typing spans, separate replay recovery and original-mode compatibility. Browser matrices guard existing shared explicit mode and existing local natural mode; the new shared mode is not exposed through Wasm/SDK/DOM yet.

contracts.admission: Guarded enable/close/insert/deletion methods each have their own documented Rust file. One-way enable retains old Undo/Redo as explicit units and authors no causal operation. Stale/read-only/non-caret/invalid requests reject atomically. Native u64 timing hints retain the local 750 ms/64-input/style/direction/separator rules; no wall-clock merging is enabled.
contracts.engineSpans: A natural burst is one explicit native engine span, not repeated Undo calls over individually recorded engine steps. Per-input forward commands, actual history keys, UI and expected effects remain retained and match ordinary explicit authoring. The first span key owns the first before-caret recipe; extensions update its after-cursors and final UI. Actual native popped keys and original-input counts mirror both stacks, including invisible contributions with no opposite item.
contracts.partialInvisibility: A key-aware repeated-Undo plan was insufficient: after a peer deletes a burst prefix, a subsequent engine call could skip that prefix and consume an unrelated older edit. The native span retracts the whole burst before another engine group is considered. Tests preserve the older edit, peer prefix and exact caret offsets 6/7 through Undo/Redo. Completely engine-invisible groups retain the original engine skip-older policy. Missing visible text alone is not proof of an engine no-op; format ownership can remain effective.
contracts.preparation: Joined InsertText/DeleteText/SetFormat commands require a permanently prepared text root and verify that preparation authors no operation. An open engine group is never paused, and infrastructure is not folded into the user span. No vendor or engine patch changes.
contracts.recovery: breditor/shared-typing-session v1 binds the existing model/original journal versions but contains separately tagged rich-replica-typing-journal v1 events and sorted unique join indices. Grouped native inverses differ from per-step inverses, so the inner events are not claimed to be a standalone original journal. Original checkpoint/restore reject enabled owners/new families instead of flattening. Original forward records, causal models/frames and writer lineage keep their meaning.
contracts.bounds: The entire new envelope retains the original 16 MiB and 1000-entry ceilings; joins and grouped-entry decoding stop at their bounds. Joins cannot cross remote/history entries or exceed 64 consecutive inputs. Typed unknown/duplicate fields, wrong bindings/room/family, invalid joins and divergent replay reject. Original journal decoding retains its original oversized-entry Error::Limit behavior. Group declarations do not attest physical input, clocks or permission.
contracts.boundaries: Effective selection/pending-style/policy, explicit action, history and remote publications close continuation. Exact duplicate frames and true no-ops retain it. Recovery starts a new burst and remains editable for host policy reapplication. Prepared writer candidates require the explicit grouped checkpoint route; ordinary peers receive unchanged atomic writer frames and retain their own history.
contracts.productScope: Shared Rust grouping is implemented; shared Wasm capability/commands/recovery, SDK/React/durable configuration and DOM input boundaries are next. The existing shared SDK still rejects natural policy rather than silently using explicit history. Original public Wasm surface remains five JS exports and 56 raw exports.

nativeChecks.supplementalScope: Strengthened the existing prepared-writer case after the full run: three original typing publications and two native Undo units export five ordinary writer frames. An unchanged explicit peer admits all five, matches document/author lineage and retains its own Undo unit. The focused case passes through both manifests; no production source changes after the full run.
nativeChecks.coverage: Both rich languages, original forward-record equivalence and existing Redo admission; Unicode/reversed/directional deletes; exact caret mapping through peer input; native 64/65 boundary; strict separate recovery and byte/collection bounds; no-op/time/format/separator/remote/read-only fences; late revision-failure atomicity; code, nested tasks/quotes and explicit hard breaks; prepared admission and ordinary-peer writer-frame interoperability.
nativeChecks.limits: The retained 65-input debug contract is deliberately complete and can take over a minute under concurrent qualification load. These are functional/debug test timings, not release latency or supported-size measurements. No performance gate or budget is approved or raised. Existing vendored HasIdSpan warning is unchanged.

installedRegression.policy: Complete discovered-file matrices, all three engines, one worker, zero retries and unchanged 60-second case/300-second process deadlines. No cherry-picking or deadline increase.
installedRegression.limitation: The new shared native grouping/recovery family is not reached by these browser cases. Shared new-mode installed keyboard, checkpoint/storage, offline/remote and future-history acceptance remains required. Native-only passes do not close that feature. No physical IME/clipboard/screen-reader claim.

failedAndIntermediateAttempts: The first six-case run passes five/fails one because formatted paragraph input retains an effective format inverse even when its text is deleted. The actual invisible case now uses the plain caption and remains strict, alongside the formatted tests. Review also reproduced a prototype regression: globally bounded old-journal parsing changed its oversized-entry Error::Limit. The regression fails before the scoped generic decoder and passes afterward; only the new family uses early bounded entry allocation. One short test command put --skip before the runner separator and did not execute tests; it was corrected. Intermediate native/research and 225/78 browser matrices passed before that parser correction, but final qualification uses rebuilt corrected archives and reruns. No failed attempt is claimed as a passing release check.
